comparator.name: International Bachelor Arts and Culture Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The official three-year, 180-EC programme approaches arts and culture through history, sociology, economics, management, policy, media, heritage and social-science research. Year 1 is common, later study provides three focus directions—Culture and Economics, Culture and Society, and Culture and Media—and the programme culminates in independent research. Culture and Society is selected neutrally as the broadest continuation of the generic target.
components: History of Western Arts and Culture
Economics, policy and organisation of arts and culture
Minor, exchange or elective profile space
Independent bachelor research project and thesis

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Art history, heritage and cultural institutions
Sociology of culture, identity and cultural participation
Qualitative and quantitative cultural research and independent inquiry
Cultural economics, policy, management and creative organisations
Media, communication, audiences and digital culture
Interdisciplinary interpretation across art, literature, history and philosophy
questions: How are arts and cultural value produced, distributed, governed and experienced?
How do globalisation, digitalisation and social change reshape culture and creative organisations?

selection.assessment: The closest match centres arts, culture and society, including history, heritage, sociology, interpretation and research. Culture and Economics and Culture and Media are both official, evidence-backed directions that UCR can represent through materially different course sets. Three alternatives are included, the maximum.

alternatives.label: Arts, culture & society
alternatives.labelReason: Art history, heritage, sociology, literature, media and historical research form a broad arts-and-culture pathway centred on society and interpretation.
alternatives.concept: A broad arts-and-culture pathway examining artistic traditions, heritage, identity, social institutions, public memory and cultural meaning.
progression: Introductory history, sociology and art history precede advanced heritage, media and research seminars. The History Research Seminar is placed after sustained historical and qualitative preparation. All courses are offered in their assigned semesters.

alternatives.label: Cultural economics, policy & creative organisations
alternatives.labelReason: The pathway joins art and heritage to economics, finance, leadership, policy and research, making cultural organisations and the creative economy its explicit centre.
alternatives.concept: A Culture and Economics direction focused on creative organisations, cultural markets, policy, audiences, funding and evidence-informed management.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest route, this curriculum replaces much of its history, literature and media sequence with economics, accounting, public economics, econometrics, behavioural economics, leadership and data science.
progression: Economics, methods and organisational foundations precede public economics, econometrics and leadership. Art-history and sociology foundations precede advanced heritage and cultural analysis. All offerings are respected.

alternatives.label: Culture, media & digital communication
alternatives.labelReason: Media history, digital platforms, environmental media, race, documentary practice and communication create a coherent Culture and Media direction.
alternatives.concept: A Culture and Media direction combining art and heritage with media history, digital culture, representation, audiences, communication and creative practice.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces the closest curriculum’s extended history and literary sequence with film and media, digital platforms, media and race, documentary, persuasive communication and creative communication.
progression: Introductory art, sociology and media precede advanced media, communication and heritage courses. Level-300 seminars are concentrated in years 2 and 3 after the relevant foundations. All courses are offered in their assigned semesters.

notes.text: UCR can create coherent interdisciplinary arts-and-culture pathways but cannot reproduce the comparator’s dedicated cultural-sector fieldwork, full focus-area menu, specialist cultural-economics sequence or supervised programme-specific thesis environment.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic IBACS degree. Of its three official directions, Culture and Society most broadly continues the common interdisciplinary academic identity and is not selected because of UCR course availability.
